verdicts.title: Published install instructions install an unrelated PyPI project instead of Opaque
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. docs/getting-started/installation.md:19-28 carry --index-url https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/simple/, but the four Extras lines at :33-36 (pip install "opaque[auditing]" / [dpftrl] / [transformers] / [all]) carry no index at all; README.md:67-73 vs :78-81 is the identical pattern. I re-ran the reproduction in a clean python3 -m venv: `pip install --dry-run --no-deps "opaque[auditing]"` resolves from PyPI and prints 'Using cached opaque-1.0.0.tar.gz (10 kB)' ... 'Would install opaque-1.0.0'. https://pypi.org/pypi/opaque/json confirms that name belongs to a different project: version 1.0.0, summary 'python libopaque wrapper', author 'Stefan Marsiske', home_page https://github.com/stef/libopaque. The unclaimed-namespace half also checks out: opaque-dpsgd, opaque-engine and opaque-base all 404 on PyPI, and opaque-accounting resolves to a metadata-less 999.9.9 placeholder. The GitHub API reports the repo as visibility 'public', and the live docs page https://jetbrains-research.github.io/opaque/latest/getting-started/installation/ returns 200. I looked for an upstream guard and found none: there is no pip.conf / global index in the docs, no note telling the reader the index applies to the whole section, and no CI scenario that executes documented install commands (ARC-011 is marked Planned). Severity stays medium rather than higher: no privacy guarantee is affected, the failure is loud at import time rather than silent, and the wrong package is a benign third-party wrapper today, not an attacker-controlled upload. It is above low because the commands are on a live public page and every extras path is broken.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A reader of the live installation page (or README) copies any of the four Extras commands. Because those lines omit --index-url, pip resolves 'opaque' from PyPI and installs opaque 1.0.0, an unrelated libopaque C-binding wrapper by Stefan Marsiske; the [auditing]/[dpftrl]/[transformers]/[all] extras are only warned about, not honored. No Opaque sub-wheel is installed, so `import opaque.dpftrl` raises ModuleNotFoundError. Verified verbatim in a fresh venv: 'Using cached opaque-1.0.0.tar.gz (10 kB)' then 'Would install opaque-1.0.0'. Secondary, not yet exploited: opaque-dpsgd / opaque-engine / opaque-base are unregistered on PyPI, so the same missing-index pattern is the shape a dependency-confusion upload would need. No privacy guarantee is affected.

verdicts.title: privacy_auditing tutorial prices a shuffled fixed-batch loop with Poisson amplification and uses the result as the audit ceiling
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced every link. docs/tutorials/privacy_auditing.ipynb code cell 9 is `train_loader = DataLoader(train_data, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True)` - shuffled fixed-size batches, no sampler - and code cell 13 prices it as `dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(noise_multiplier), sample_rate) * total_steps` and prints it as 'Theoretical epsilon', then compares the audited epsilon against it. Poisson amplification requires independent per-record inclusion; it does not hold for a shuffled fixed-batch partition, so the conservative analysis for that loop is unamplified composition. I ran the notebook's own setup with the shipped code (torch 2.14, .venv): coin_flip(key=key(42), num_canaries=500) leaves len(train_data)=252, so sample_rate=0.25397 and the notebook's total_steps=200*(252//64)=600. With the shipped accountant, poisson eps at delta=1e-5 = 250.886 and unamplified gaussian(0.5)*600 = 1408.936 (the finding's 1408.936 matches exactly; its 253.2 came from assuming 250 train examples). I additionally found an error the finding missed and which makes it worse: with 252 examples, batch_size=64 and DataLoader's default drop_last=False the loop performs ceil(252/64)=4 releases per epoch, i.e. 800 steps, while total_steps counts 252//64=3 per epoch, i.e. 600. The conservative bound for the loop as actually written is therefore gaussian(0.5)*800 = 1841.258, a 7.3x understatement of the published 250.886. I checked for sibling code paths that would excuse it: the other three tutorials (dp_sgd_training, sampling_and_microbatching, distributed_training, llm_finetuning) all construct PoissonSampler and pass it as batch_sampler, and dp_sgd_training cell 13 was rewritten by 12146ec4 with the comment 'The sampler and accountant use the same independent-inclusion process' - so privacy_auditing.ipynb is the only remaining notebook with this mismatch, and .github/workflows/pr.yml:294-301 executes only three notebooks, none of them this one. One sub-claim I could not sustain and have dropped from the scenario: the finding argues the `p - (lr / bs) * g` update leaks because bs is 'a data-dependent quantity the mechanism never noised'. Under the fixed shuffled partition used here bs is deterministic per step (64,64,64,60), so it is just a per-step learning-rate scale, not a data-dependent release; that objection applies to the Poisson-sampled notebooks, not this one. Severity medium, not high: the library code is correct, this is a synthetic tutorial whose epsilon is meaninglessly large either way (250 vs 1841), and the printed 'OK' line still holds numerically because the audited epsilon is far below both bounds. It is not low because the number is published on the live docs site as the 'theoretical' guarantee and the pattern is the one a reader copies.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: docs/tutorials/privacy_auditing.ipynb trains with a shuffled fixed-batch DataLoader (cell 9) but prices the run with Poisson subsampling amplification (cell 13) and labels the result 'Theoretical epsilon'. With the notebook's own parameters (noise_multiplier=0.5, clipping_norm=1.0, batch_size=64, n_epochs=200, len(train_data)=252 after coin_flip) it publishes 250.886 at delta=1e-5. The defensible bound for the loop as written is unamplified composition over the releases actually performed: the loop emits ceil(252/64)=4 releases per epoch (800 total) while total_steps counts only 3 (600), so the conservative bound is gaussian(0.5)*800 = 1841.258 - a 7.3x understatement (5.6x from the amplification error alone at the accounted 600 steps). No library code is wrong and the audit's 'OK' comparison still holds numerically; the harm is a published epsilon a reader cannot justify and a shuffled-DataLoader-plus-Poisson-accountant pattern that the other four tutorials deliberately avoid.

verdicts.title: Sweep A's executable-docs gate executes no Markdown snippet and only 3 of 7 notebooks
verdicts.reasoning: Every factual claim checks out. .github/workflows/pr.yml:290-301 'Execute accounting documentation' runs exactly `uv run python examples/quickstart.py`, `uv run python -m doctest packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/accounting/__init__.py`, and a loop over accounting_and_calibration.ipynb / dp_sgd_training.ipynb / dp_ftrl_training.ipynb. My own scan of docs/**/*.md counts 369 ```python fences across 46 files, and a grep over .github/workflows shows the only execution verbs anywhere are those three lines - nothing executes a Markdown fence. mkdocs.yml:137-145 lists 7 tutorial notebooks; the 4 not in the loop are sampling_and_microbatching, llm_finetuning, privacy_auditing and distributed_training (finding 61 is a live defect in one of them, which is the strongest support for this finding). docs/getting-started/quickstart.md:11 does transclude the executed script via `--8<-- "examples/quickstart.py:4:"`. .github/workflows/docs.yml fires on push to main and runs only `uv sync --group docs` then `mike deploy` - no --strict build, no examples group, no execution step, and no dependency on ci.yml. `git show --stat 12146ec4` confirms Sweep A hand-edited 11 Markdown files (docs/user-guide/accounting.md, sampling.md, dp-sgd.md, docs/reference/*.md, ...) whose snippets the new gate does not cover, so 'executes zero of the snippets the Sweep A findings were about' is accurate. Two things I downgrade. First, the cited 'live instance that survived Sweep A' - `optimizer.step(noisy_grads)` at docs/reference/rng.md:325 - sits in an illustrative block with undefined `model`, `batch`, `compute_dp_grads` and `optimizer`; it is pseudocode, not a snippet any executable-docs gate would have run, so it is not evidence that the gate missed something runnable. Second, the docs.yml half is largely theoretical: pushes to main come from PRs that already ran the strict build, so an unchecked deploy needs a direct push. Severity drops to low: this is a coverage/completeness gap against a closed issue's acceptance criteria rather than a defect in shipped code or a live wrong result; its one concrete consequence is already reported separately as finding 61, and double-counting it here would inflate it. It belongs as a follow-up under the still-open CI/test-integrity umbrella (#774) or docs umbrella (#775), neither of which tracks this specific gap today.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: The executable-docs step added by 12146ec4 (.github/workflows/pr.yml:290-301) covers examples/quickstart.py, one doctest module, and 3 of the 7 tutorial notebooks in mkdocs.yml. It executes none of the 369 ```python fences in the 46 Markdown files under docs/, including the 11 Markdown files Sweep A itself hand-edited, and none of the 4 remaining notebooks. So a future signature change can drift a documented accounting snippet while `mkdocs build --strict` (which does not execute code) and the notebook loop both pass. This is a gate-coverage gap, not a defect in shipped code; its one currently live consequence is the Poisson-vs-shuffled mismatch in docs/tutorials/privacy_auditing.ipynb, reported separately. Additionally .github/workflows/docs.yml deploys the public site on push to main with `mike deploy` and neither --strict nor any execution step, so a direct push to main could publish an unchecked site.

verdicts.title: Per-group Gaussian noise has no realized-vs-reported conformance test
verdicts.reasoning: The coverage claim is true; the risk framing is overstated and I corrected it. Confirmed: OPQ-378's fix sketch (scratchpad NEW-FINDINGS-MASTER-LIST.md:574) names 'gaussian_noise, per-group gaussian_noise and mf_gaussian_noise', and 31ffed65 (PR #871, 'test(noise): add stddev conformance coverage') touched only packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/noise/test_noise.py (one scalar case at :133-142 using the new _assert_realized_stddev_matches_reported helper) and packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/noise/test_realized_stddev.py (the MF strategies). A grep for 'realized' across the dpsgd, dpftrl and engine test trees finds no per-group case, so no test binds realized per-group noise magnitude to the reported PerGroup. The only magnitude assertion for the per-group path is packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/noise/test_per_group_noise.py:46-49, `assert mlp_var > attn_var * 2.5` over 100-element tensors, which is indeed invariant to a uniform scale factor. Where the finding overreaches: I read the implementation (packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/noise/_gaussian.py, `_add_noise_tree` per-group branch and the `noise_stddev=effective_stddev` publication) and the applied and reported values are the same object, so divergence requires a bug inside `_sample` or `PerGroup.for_path`. `_sample` is shared with the scalar path and is therefore already pinned by the new scalar conformance test; `per_group_noise_stddev`'s output is pinned exactly by test_per_group_noise.py's `noise_stddev.values == sqrt(6), sqrt(30)`; and a path-misresolution bug in `for_path` collapses the two groups' variances and so is caught by the existing 2.5x ratio assertion (reported variance ratio is 5). The finding's mutation only evades the suite because it is conditional on the caller frame being `_add_noise_tree`, which no real source edit can express. I also verified there is no live defect: at noise_multiplier=1.5 with PerGroup{attn:1.0, mlp:5.0} over 5e5-element leaves, realized RMS / reported for_path ratios are 0.9998 and 1.0005, and stay within 0.15% for bfloat16, float16 and float64 leaves. So this is a genuine but narrow test-coverage debt, not a latent wrong-noise bug. Severity stays at low (the category floor); the incomplete-delivery-against-fix-sketch observation is what makes it worth one line, not any reachable failure. OPQ-378's issue (#833) is closed and is not in the 2026-09-13 open sets, so this is not a duplicate of open work.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: No live defect: I measured realized-vs-reported per-group stddev directly and it matches to within 0.15% for float32, bfloat16, float16 and float64 leaves. The established gap is test coverage only. PR #871 delivered the realized-vs-reported conformance assertion for scalar gaussian_noise and for the six mf_gaussian_noise strategies but not for the per-group path named in OPQ-378's fix sketch, and no other test ties realized per-group noise magnitude to output.noise_stddev.for_path(...). The one per-group magnitude assertion (test_per_group_noise.py:46-49, mlp_var > attn_var * 2.5 over 100 samples) is invariant to a uniform scale error. The exposure is narrower than the finding claims: a uniform scale error would have to originate in per-group-only code between the stddev computation and the draw, and the only such code is the PerGroup lookup, whose realistic failure (misresolving a leaf to the wrong group) collapses the variance ratio and is already caught. The residual risk is a future per-group-only cast or rescale (for example a device/dtype or world-size adjustment added to that branch) shipping green. Fix remains cheap: one PerGroup case in the existing _assert_realized_stddev_matches_reported helper, plus one for the paired second-moment streams.
